conceptZh: 胖胖的玩具鳥把「天」的短橫當成天空中的停棲處，努力收腳站穩，卻被小雲朵接走。
object: A solid blue 天, a round wind-up toy bird, and a small floating cloud cushion.
morph: The glyph remains correctly formed and stationary; its shorter upper horizontal becomes a temporary perch for the toy bird.
creativeAngle: 不再用雲壓成筆畫；讓完整字形先出現，以胖鳥擠上短橫、失去平衡後被雲接住的尺寸反差製造笑點。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated toy-world video teaching the Traditional Chinese glyph 天, meaning sky. Use a locked frontal camera, a pale cream-blue sky background, soft lighting, and bright, non-neon colors. From the first frame, display one correctly formed, saturated cobalt-blue 天 centered and uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Preserve its shorter upper horizontal, longer lower horizontal, and correctly joined left-falling and right-falling strokes. Keep every stroke fixed and clearly readable throughout.

At 0.3 seconds, a plump wind-up toy bird with tiny hinged wings descends toward the short upper horizontal. Its feet initially spread wider than the perch; it looks down and comically shuffles them inward until they fit. At 2.2 seconds, pause briefly as it proudly balances. Its round body then gently tips backward, feet pointing upward. A small fluffy animated cloud cushion immediately catches it above the glyph with a soft cushion squeak. The bird settles into the cloud like an absurdly comfortable armchair and gives one satisfied wing wiggle. The cloud carries it out through the upper-right edge by 4.5 seconds. Stage this action above the upper horizontal without covering or changing the strokes. Hold the solitary, centered glyph completely still from 4.5 to 8.0 seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “天、天、天空”. Say the first 天 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 1.5 seconds, and 天空 naturally around 5.3 seconds during the clear final hold. Use the usual ㄊㄧㄢ pronunciation. Stop speaking after 天空. Keep the gentle toy sounds below the voice; use no music. Only the single target glyph 天 appears as on-screen text, with no vocabulary text, subtitles, other lettering, watermark, clutter, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 積木小隊想疊高摸天空，隊長卻原地踏步，把整座高塔震成一團；大家重新合作，鋪成清楚的「天」。
object: An original squad of expressive cobalt-blue interlocking building bricks
morph: After their sky-reaching tower collapses, the bricks crawl and interlock into four continuous strokes: a short upper horizontal, a longer lower horizontal, and two correctly connected descending strokes.
creativeAngle: 改用積木小隊挑戰疊高：最上面的隊長得意踏步，整隊卻像手風琴逐層縮下，最後隊長踩到自己的底座。笑點來自逞強與高度落差，再以慢而明確的合作組字收尾。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animated video teaching the Traditional Chinese character 天, meaning sky. Use a locked frontal camera, a pale powder-blue background, a subtly curved cream floor, and soft, bright lighting. The original lead is a squad of cobalt-blue interlocking building bricks with tiny expressive faces and retractable feet: earnestly disciplined, comically overconfident, and ultimately cooperative. Keep the central teaching action fully visible with generous margins.

At the opening, the squad is already marching up its own compact staircase, stacking into a tall, narrow tower as though determined to reach the sky. By 1.4 seconds, the topmost captain proudly looks upward and performs two unnecessary marching stamps. Hold a tiny anticipation pause: every brick below glances up. From 2.0 to 3.1 seconds, the stamps make the tower fold downward in a rapid, harmless accordion collapse, one tier after another. The captain keeps marching during the descent and suddenly finds itself stepping on the original bottom brick at floor level. It freezes mid-step, looks down, then looks straight up at all the empty sky it has lost. Use soft hollow toy clacks, never a startling crash.

From 3.3 to 4.7 seconds, the captain sheepishly lowers its foot and joins the squad. In one continuous, readable assembly, the bricks crawl outward, tip onto their sides, and interlock into a single upright, front-facing 天. Use a correct standard Traditional Chinese glyph silhouette as the assembly template. Clearly establish the short upper horizontal and the longer horizontal beneath it; the left-falling stroke begins at the upper central junction and passes through the lower horizontal, while the right-falling stroke branches at the proper central junction and opens toward the lower right. Shape the brick chains to follow these strokes precisely, with no central head, extra vertical stem, gaps, or protruding studs. As connections finish, feet and faces retract and seams become visually flush, leaving four crisp, continuous saturated-blue strokes.

From 4.7 through 8.0 seconds, hold the completed 天 completely still, centered, uncropped, and approximately 70% of frame height. Preserve clear negative spaces and comfortable margins. The finished glyph is the only remaining foreground form.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “天、天、天空”. Pronounce the first 天 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 1.4 seconds, and 天空 around 5.5 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly held. Use the usual ㄊㄧㄢ reading and stop after 天空. Keep toy sound effects below the voice; use no music. Display only the single target glyph 天 as text, with no vocabulary text, subtitles, other lettering, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
